title: serving-runtime-weekly-update-kernel-kv-batching-2026-10-21
content:
Serving Runtime - Weekly Update (kernel work, KV cache, batching)
Week of 2026-10-21
Owner: Asha Patel (eng-serving-runtime)
Collaborators: Liam Chen, Riley Morgan, Samir Gupta, Evelyn Park
Status: in_review

Summary / Highlights:
- Kernel optimizations: landed a new fused attention kernel prototype on x86+Ampere (PR #894), showing 8-12% p50 token latency reduction for long-context models (8k-16k). The fused kernel path still gated behind runtime toggle.
- KV cache sharding: PoC for multi-GPU KV sharding merged to feature branch (RINF-1423). End-to-end tests show ~1.9x effective KV capacity for 4x A100 nodes with negligible p95 regression when prefetching is warm.
- Dynamic batching: New adaptive thresholding experiment (batch_min=4, batch_target_latency=60ms) reduced tail latency on low-concurrency workloads while maintaining throughput for high-concurrency requesters.

Details / Notes:
1) Kernel work (Liam + Samir)
  - What we did: Implemented fused QKV + attention softmax kernel for FP16 path with improved memory layout (NCHW->packed QKV). Added micro-bench harness and CI perf job.
  - Results: On internal Llama-70B-ish benchmark (seq_len=8192, batch=1-4): p50 token latency down 8% on p4d, 10-12% on A100. Throughput for batch>=8 unchanged. p95 improved 3-5% after small launchpad fixes.
  - Risks / open items: numerical diffs (small) in a few attention corner cases; Samir to file a follow-up refactor to align FP32 fallback. See PR: https://github.com/redwood/re/runtime/pull/894 and ticket RINF-1478.
  - Blockers: need wider OSS-style review and perf regression guard in CI.

2) KV cache (Riley + Evelyn)
  - What we did: Completed sharding PoC where KV shards are horizontally partitioned across GPUs and an async prefetch pipeline warms destination GPU cache before attention stage. Added metrics for remote-prefetch hit rate and stall time.
  - Results: With prefetch warmed, effective max context grows ~1.9x for 4-GPU setups. Observed a 4-7ms added jitter when prefetch misses occur; average request path unaffected when hit-rate > 0.85.
  - Tradeoffs: Network overhead for prefetch, additional memory bookkeeping. We reduced metadata overhead by compressing shard map entries.
  - Next step: Run cluster-scale soak on staging for 72h (Riley), then enable canary on Dedicated for a subset of customers (Evelyn + SRE). Linked Confluence design: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/RINF/kv-cache-sharding and ticket RINF-1423.

3) Batching and scheduler (Asha + infra)
  - What we did: Deployed adaptive batching config to staging: dynamic threshold with a latency-based backoff. Added backpressure signal from runtime to frontend to avoid queue buildup for tight-SLO customers.
  - Results: For low qps single-tenant tests, tail latency p95 improved 18% while overall token throughput +/-2%. For multi-tenant, burst resilience improved, but some pacing tweaks needed for very bursty traffic.
  - Action: Adjust batch_size floor from 2->4 for chat workloads; evaluate cost impact on tokens/sec. Ticket RINF-1501 open for tuning.

Metrics / Observability:
- Perf dashboards: token-latency-p50/p95 (model: redwood-8k); staging baseline vs kernel-fused branch.
- Current numbers (staging): baseline p50=22ms/token, fused-kernel p50=19.8ms/token. p95 baseline=65ms, fused=61ms.
- KV prefetch metrics: prefetch_hit_rate=0.87 (staging), average_prefetch_latency=3.8ms, prefetch_stall_count=12/1M requests.
- Batching: average_batch_size=5.6 (chat), queue_wait_ms p95 down from 48ms -> 31ms.

Standup / Daily log (this week)
- Mon 10/19: Kernel fused prototype landed in feature branch. Started CI perf job. (Liam)
- Tue 10/20: KV prefetch PoC merged; found a memory leak in metadata map, fixed by Evelyn. Started 12h soak. (Riley/Evelyn)
- Wed 10/21: Adaptive batching experiment results in staging; initial tuning shows batch_min=4 is better for chat. Launching longer run. (Asha)
- Thu 10/22: Repro on a numerical diff for fused kernel for some FP32 fallbacks; Samir to investigate - small precision mismatch on odd seq lengths. (Samir)
- Fri 10/23: Planning canary for KV sharding on Dedicated; synced with SRE and solutions-eng for rollback plan. (Riley/Evelyn/SRE)

Blockers / Risks:
- Kernel numerical diffs: need to ensure parity for regression analyzer to avoid model quality regressions (ticket RINF-1478).
- KV prefetch cold-miss jitter: must keep prefetch hit-rate high; otherwise we risk customer-visible jitter. Need better heuristics for when to prefetch.
- CI perf noise: current CI environment has variance; we need controlled racks on dedicated infra for reliable perf baselining.

Action items / Owners:
- Samir: debug FP32 fallback numerical diff for fused kernel; aim to have PR by 2026-10-28. (RINF-1478)
- Riley: run 72h staging soak of KV sharding with multiple model families (due 2026-10-27).
- Evelyn: prepare canary rollout plan + rollback playbook for Dedicated; coordinate with SRE and Customer Success (due 2026-10-29).
- Asha: finalize adaptive batching tuning and submit RINF-1501 with recommended defaults by 2026-10-25.
- Liam: add perf regression guard and deterministic microbench harness to CI (due 2026-10-30).

Meeting notes / decisions:
- 10/20 Kernel sync: agreed to gate fused kernel behind runtime flag and run A/B canary (10% traffic) once numeric parity verified.
- 10/21 KV design review: approved sharding approach; require SLO guardrails and increased observability before canary. Confluence doc updated.

Relevant links / refs:
- PR: https://github.com/redwood/re/runtime/pull/894
- Design: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/RINF/kv-cache-sharding
- Tickets: RINF-1423, RINF-1478, RINF-1501
- Slack threads: #kernel-optimizations-thread, #kv-cache-ops (see thread pins)

Notes / To follow up:
- Confirm end-to-end perf on p4d racks under realistic multi-tenant traffic (Samir + Liam).
- Explore small-quantization friendly kernel variants for INT8 paths in parallel (research spike).
- Consider exposing a customer-level toggle for KV prefetch aggressiveness for Dedicated customers with tighter latency SLOs.

Archived attachments: test logs, microbench csvs, and perf dashboard snapshots attached to Confluence page above.

This is a working doc; expect iterative updates. Ping in slack if you want an ad-hoc review.
